a1
After the flood, Noah's three sons had children of their own.
b1
From Japheth came the peoples of the coastlands, each with their own land and language.
b2
From Ham came Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan, and their many families.
c1
Among Cush's descendants was Nimrod, the first mighty warrior on earth.
c2
Scripture calls him a mighty hunter before the Lord, and his kingdom began in Babel.
c3
He went on to Assyria, and built Nineveh and other great cities.
d1
Then Genesis turns to Shem, the older brother of Japheth.
d2
Through Shem came Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
d3
Arpachshad's line led to Eber, whose sons were Peleg and Joktan.
d4
In Peleg's days, the earth was divided.
e1
Family after family, nation after nation, they spread across the earth.
e2
The chapter ends with one clear line: from Noah's sons, the nations spread after the flood.
h1
Genesis 10 is a long list of names, but it holds one truth.
h2
Every nation, language, and people comes from one human family.
h3
So no one is a stranger to God. Before you judge someone, remember they share your origin.
h4
Today, treat one person like family.
i
Who have you been treating as a stranger?
